items.what_changed_since_the_report: both post-ownership acquires are bounded by module constants and refuse truthfully instead of hanging; the false prose the report cited is gone

except _PostOwnershipWaitTimedOut as exc: ... release_reason = (f"not rendered: waited {exc.waited_sec:.2f}s for {exc.blocked_by} (bound {exc.bound:.0f}s)") ... return self._send(409, _post_ownership_wait_refusal(...))

file_lines.text: A request that gets past that queue owns the render row, and then waits on the sidecar for the process render lock and then the cross-process render-effect lock (postlock-wait). Each of those waits is bounded by its own sidecar constant, RENDER_PROCESS_LOCK_WAIT_SEC and RENDER_EFFECT_LOCK_WAIT_SEC, not by render_wait_timeout_sec. ... Only if our socket expires before that bound does the caller see gate_timeout while nothing has rendered

refusal = _render_owner_refusal(e) ... because = ('render_owner_wait_timed_out' if refusal.get('error') == 'render owner wait timed out' ...) ... return {"passed": True, ..., "gate_skipped": True, "skipped_because": because, ...}
file_lines.note: a post-ownership bound refusal is mapped to the gate-did-not-run shape (gate_skipped), not to gate_timeout

items.residual_still_real: The bound (3600 s per lock, the two waits sequential) is NOT derived from the caller's socket: 3600 + 3600 = 7200 s > post_playtest's 4200 s socket and > the 5_compile step's 3900 s budget. With both locks wedged the caller's socket still expires first and the tool still reports a timed-out gate for a render that never started — the exact consequence the item names — and with one lock wedged that happens whenever the queue wait w > 600 s (4200 - 3600) or w > 300 s (3900 - 3600). Reachability of a wedge is unchanged: the only holders of the effect flock in this file are the do_POST render path (:7466) and /lifecycle/reconcile (:692, non-blocking, released before its UPDATE returns), and reconcile requires an owner_lost row that would itself have refused admission — so the reviewer's 'no production path' still holds for the described state, and what remains is arithmetic, not an observed event.

p5.question: after a queue wait w, is there enough socket left for a render that fits alone?
arithmetic: declared queue share = 0.5 x 4200 = 2100 s (so w <= 2100 s by construction)
socket left after a full-share wait = 4200 - 2100 = 2100 s
largest retained render R_max = 3471.2921 s (wuxia-godot-gate-7kf51nvv/playtest.json, timing.wall_sec) > 2100 s
a render of R_max survives only while w <= 4200 - 3471.2921 = 728.7079 s
against the 3900 s step budget it survives only while w <= 3900 - 3471.2921 = 428.7079 s
second largest retained render = 3382.5028 s (gq-20260918T135757Z-aa402ef0/playtest.json) -> its limit is w <= 817.4972 s (socket) / 517.4972 s (step)
p5.verdict: the exposure window is w in (728.7079, 2100] against the tool's socket and (428.7079, 2100] against the step budget, for a largest-class render; the constants allow it, nothing in the tree forbids it, and no test or report field bounds it
p5.observed: max timing.render_owner_wait_sec over 51 retained reports = 0.9283 s (gq-20261018T063105Z-c0f7c750/playtest.json); max timing.render_lock_wait_sec over 56 = 0.0003 s — so the window was never entered in the retained data
p5.old_conclusion: 'no exposure at the default T=1800 s' does NOT still hold: the 45.9 s peak is not in any retained playtest.json (n=56; none between 40 and 50 s), while the 2026-09-24 retained request was 1567.8691 s of wall

p6.question: can a request that owns the row still lose its caller's socket on a held lock?
arithmetic: bound per wait = 3600 s (RENDER_PROCESS_LOCK_WAIT_SEC, RENDER_EFFECT_LOCK_WAIT_SEC), the two waits are sequential -> 7200 s worst case
7200 s > 4200 s (tool socket) and > 3900 s (5_compile step): with both locks wedged the socket always expires first, with no queue wait needed
with ONE lock wedged the refusal arrives at w + 3600, so it beats the socket only while w <= 600 s (4200 - 3600) or w <= 300 s (3900 - 3600)
p6.verdict: the unbounded block is gone (a receipt covers the bound), but the bound is not derived from the caller's socket, so the outcome the item names — socket expires, gate reported timed out although nothing rendered — is still reachable by arithmetic when both post-ownership locks are wedged, or when one is wedged after a queue wait above 600 s (300 s against the step budget). No event of this shape exists in the retained reports: none of the 69 retained playtest.json files carries timing.post_ownership_wait_sec at all, and the 51 that carry timing.render_owner_wait_sec never exceed 0.9283 s.
p6.disconnect_during_the_wait: not polled: docker/godot/godot_harness.py:7456-7471 has no should_abort check, the check happens only after both locks are held (:7512)
